event: Determine the direction of a creak and thud sound (door closing) relative to a hypothetical robot's position and orientation.

sounding_object.description: The arched wooden front door. It is dark brown wood, with an arched top. It has a small, narrow rectangular window with a decorative metal grille. Standard exterior door height and width.

reference_object.description: A tall, dark brown wooden china cabinet with glass doors on the upper section displaying china/dishes, and solid wood doors/drawers on the lower section. Approximately 2 meters tall and 1-1.2 meters wide.

facing_object.object_name: Light-gray armchair closer to the wall painting
facing_object.description: A light-gray upholstered armchair with wooden legs. It is one of two identical armchairs situated under a large arched window. This specific armchair is the one positioned more towards the wall painting (which is on the same wall segment as the fireplace, to the right of a white interior door).

question: Imagine you are a robot standing by the wooden china cabinet and facing the light-gray armchair closer to the wall painting, when the creak and thud sound comes up, relative to where you are facing, where is the sounding object: left, right, or back? If the object is generally to your left and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees left, choose 'left'. If the object is generally to your right and facing it requires turning less than 120 degrees right, choose 'right'. If the object is generally behind you and facing it requires turning 120 degrees or more, choose 'back'.
